decisions.executionNote: Raise and pitch right wrist toward basket with small continuous elbow-up increments; left stays at origin.
Advance above basket and pitch fingers downward toward the rear-left egg, leaving clearance.
Align on the nearer left egg and descend slowly; verify fingertip-to-egg alignment before closing.
Make a small near-egg correction, close fully, and start a short lift to test retention visually.
Lift vertically with closure maintained to check whether an egg is retained.
Empty grasp observed. Reopen and approach the rear-left egg more vertically, correcting the grasp height.
Lower around the visible rear-left egg, then close fully while holding the wrist stationary.
Lift the enclosed egg clear of the basket while keeping the right gripper fully closed; check retention.
Carry the visibly retained egg toward the holder at clearance height, angling inward while keeping the right wrist in its workspace.
Continue carrying toward the holder's right-side cup with a gradual inward wrist angle; keep egg closed and above the rim.
Egg appears released over the holder; open and clear the rim while checking where it settles.
One egg is visibly seated in the front-right cup. Return above the basket for the next egg, reopening and restoring downward approach.
Position the open right gripper above the remaining rear egg with downward fingers, descending to a visual alignment height.
Refine toward the rear egg seen right of the wrist center, lower around its sides, then close fully for a retention test.
Maintain full closure around the centered egg and begin a short vertical lift, checking visual retention before transfer.
Continue a slow vertical retention test with full closure; avoid lateral transfer until the egg clears the basket.
Egg slipped back into basket. Reopen and correct leftward over its new location; descend for a deeper centered grasp.
Egg is centered between open fingertips. Lower slightly to enclose its sides, close fully, and pause before lifting.
Lift straight up with full closure commanded; inspect whether the deeply enclosed egg follows the gripper.
Egg follows the gripper and two remain in the basket. Carry toward the rear-right cup at clearance height with gradual inward tilt.
Continue toward the empty rear-right cup, lowering gradually while retaining the egg and keeping the wrist right of center.
Align the retained egg over the rear-right cavity and lower toward its bottom, preserving grasp orientation and right-side wrist clearance.
Lid proximity limits descent. Release the egg directly over the rear-right cup, then retract up and forward to clear the lid and inspect settling.
Two eggs now appear seated, rear-left and front-right. Return toward the basket with the gripper open to retrieve the third.
Approach the right-hand remaining egg with an open downward gripper, stopping above the grasp height for visual alignment.
Tracking was interrupted near the basket rim. Replan from observed pose: lift clear first, then move right in smaller increments.
Clear of the rim, align above the right remaining egg and descend with the current near-vertical orientation.
Center the third egg between the fingers, descend around its sides, and close fully before lifting.
Lift straight up with full closure commanded to verify third-egg retention and clear the basket before transfer.
Third egg visibly follows the gripper; carry inward at clearance height with full closure and a gradual tilt toward the holder.
Carry the retained third egg over the empty rear-right cavity, approaching slowly from the right while keeping clear of the lid.
Third egg slipped onto the table between basket and holder. Reopen and align vertically above its visible resting position for recovery.
Descend vertically over the table egg with jaws open, checking centering before a deeper recovery grasp.
Lower the open fingers around the table egg and close fully while stationary for a centered recovery grasp.
Recovery grasp contacted only the egg tip. Reopen, follow its near-side shift, and lower the fingers farther around the egg before closing.
Descent was obstructed near the table. Replan from actual pose, lift slightly, and shift toward the egg's visible near-side position before trying again.
The table egg is now centered between open fingers. Lower minimally and close fully without lateral motion.
Lift the centered recovered egg vertically with full closure maintained, without changing grasp angle.
Recovered egg is visibly retained. Carry slowly toward the vacant rear-right cup using only a modest inward tilt to reduce slippage.
Shift the retained egg over the rear-right cup at constant height, keeping the wrist right of center and avoiding the lid.
The retained egg appears aligned above the vacant rear-right cup. Lower minimally, release over the cavity, then lift clear to inspect settling.
Withdraw the open gripper up and right from the lid so the released egg can settle and the holder can be inspected.
Third egg appears perched near the lid hinge rather than seated. Bring closed fingertips above its far side for a gentle nearward nudge into the empty cup.
Gently lower and sweep the closed fingertips toward the near side to roll the perched egg off the hinge into the rear-right cavity.
The egg remains perched. Clear the lid by backing toward the near side and pitch the open gripper forward for access from in front rather than behind the lid.
Approach the perched egg from the front with open fingers, lower gently around it, then close for a short nearward repositioning.
Draw the enclosed perched egg a short distance toward the near side over the rear-right cavity, release, and lift clear.
Keep the gripper fully open briefly for settling, then retract up and right to remove fingertip support and inspect the rear-right cup.
Egg remains near the hinge. Approach from the near side at a lower height with open fingers to reach its sides rather than above it.
Adjust the approach from in front: back the wrist away from the lid while pitching fingertips forward and lowering gently.
The third egg appears to have moved into the rear-right cup. Withdraw the open fingers upward and rightward to verify it remains seated.
Three eggs are visibly seated. Return above the last basket egg, restoring a downward approach while keeping clearance.
Align over the last egg with near-vertical fingers while staying above the basket rim.
Descend with open fingers over the last egg, making a small forward centering correction before closing.
Correct toward the last egg's near-left position, lower around its sides, and close fully while stationary.
Lift the last egg vertically with full closure commanded, checking that it remains between the fingers before lateral transfer.
Last egg remains between the fingers and the basket appears empty. Carry toward the front-left cavity with full closure and gradual inward tilt.
Last egg slipped onto the table. Reopen and approach its visible resting position vertically for a deeper centered recovery grasp.
The loose egg rolled leftward. Track its latest visible position with open fingers while remaining above the table.
The last egg has stopped near the gripper. Descend with a small leftward correction, keeping fingers open for a centered recovery grasp.
Center the egg's broad sides at the finger pads, lower minimally, and close fully while stationary.
Lift the recovered last egg without rotating. The lid has fallen nearly closed, so begin bringing the left arm up to reopen it while the right retains the egg.
Hold the last egg steady in the right gripper. Approach the closed lid's front lip from the left workspace with the left fingers open.
Continue the left-hand approach to the front lid tab with open fingers; keep the right-held egg stationary and separated.
Attempt to enclose the front lid tab with the left fingers and test a small upward lift; right keeps the final egg steady.
Test whether the left fingers have captured the lid by lifting slowly; keep the final egg stationary in the right hand.
Left lift did not capture the lid. Reopen and reposition lower and nearer to reach the front lip, while the right hand holds the egg stationary.
Front latch is now visible between left fingers. Advance gently to enclose the tab and close; right maintains the egg grasp.
Test the left tab grasp with a slow upward arc while maintaining closure; hold the final egg steady in the right hand.
The tab was not retained. Reopen, advance slightly farther around the front lip at its height, and close again while the right egg remains stationary.
Test an upward and slightly forward motion at the lid's front edge with the left fingers closed; keep the retained egg motionless.
